reason: In C, variable declaration explicitly requires specifying a data type to allocate and interpret memory; a student cannot define or understand variables without understanding data types.
Pointers hold the memory addresses of variables; understanding variables and how values are stored in memory is strictly necessary before learning address-of operations and pointer dereferencing.
Conditional statements rely on evaluating expressions using relational and logical operators to make branching decisions during execution.

C lacks a native primitive string type and implements strings as null-terminated character arrays; understanding array indexing, memory contiguous layout, and sizing is strictly necessary to comprehend C strings.
Structures are user-defined composite data types; understanding what built-in data types represent is conceptually required before creating custom grouped data types.
